THE RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.full:
*SYNOPSIS:* One year later, Adaeze wants to risk everything to be a human wife for one night. But the River God's first wife, Mamala, wants to kill her, Amara wants to steal Emeka, and little Zara is dying.

*FULL STORY:*

*NARRATOR:* It was the anniversary night. The night Adaeze became the River Bride. Inside the river palace, Adaeze sat on her throne, crying. Her crown was heavy.

*RIVER GOD:* Adaeze, you are crying again. Tonight you can go to land. But I warned you. If you go to see that boy, I will not allow you to come back. You will die as a human.

*ADAEZE:* Then let me die. I don't want to be a goddess forever. I want to be a wife for one night.

*NARRATOR:* Inside the deeper part of the river, someone was listening. It was MAMALA, the first wife of the River God. She was very beautiful, but her heart was full of jealousy.

*MAMALA:* (Angry) So this small human girl wants to leave our world? Good. Tonight, I will make sure she never returns. I will drown her boyfriend and kill her.

*NARRATOR:* On land, in Umunzu village, Emeka was waiting by the river. He had not married for two years. His best friend, OKONKWO, came to meet him.

*OKONKWO:* Emeka, my brother, you are here again? It is midnight. This girl is now a goddess. Forget her.

*EMEKA:* I can never forget her, Okonkwo. She said she would come every year. I will wait.

*OKONKWO:* And what about AMARA? That girl loves you. She brings you food every day. She is a good girl.

*EMEKA:* My heart belongs to Adaeze only.

*NARRATOR:* In another part of the village, AMARA was watching them from behind a tree. She was crying.

*AMARA:* Emeka, I have loved you for three years. Why can't you see me? Tonight, I will follow you to the river. I will make sure Adaeze leaves you alone.

*NARRATOR:* At midnight, the water began to spin. Adaeze came out, wearing her white wrapper, shining like moonlight. She was still 19.

*EMEKA:* Adaeze! You came!

*ADAEZE:* Emeka!

*NARRATOR:* They hugged. But before they could talk, they heard a small voice crying. It was LITTLE ZARA, the 7-year-old girl, coughing near the river bank.

*ADAEZE:* Zara? What are you doing here at night? You are burning with fever!

*LITTLE ZARA:* Mama Adaeze, I am sick. My mother said only the river goddess can save me. Please help me.

*ADAEZE:* Oh no. River God said if I touch any human tonight, I will lose my powers.

*EMEKA:* We must save her, Adaeze.

*ADAEZE:* (Touches Zara's head and prays) River, please heal this child.

*NARRATOR:* Immediately, Zara's fever disappeared. But inside the river, MAMALA felt it.

*MAMALA:* She used her power on land! Now she is weak! This is my chance.

*NARRATOR:* Suddenly, the river became rough. A big wave came out. MAMALA appeared, with snakes in her hair.

*MAMALA:* Adaeze! You are a selfish bride! You healed a human child without permission! You have broken the river law! Now you must die!

*ADAEZE:* Who are you?

*MAMALA:* I am Mamala! The first wife! The queen before you came! Tonight, I will take your life and take your boyfriend!

*EMEKA:* Leave her alone!

*OKONKWO:* (Running with his cutlass) Emeka! What is happening?

*NARRATOR:* Mamala raised her hand and the water held Emeka and Okonkwo, so they could not move.

*MAMALA:* You cannot fight me, humans!

*NARRATOR:* Adaeze was afraid and weak. She was about to give up. Then, a soft light appeared on the water. It was a woman in white. It was NGOZI, Adaeze's mother who died many years ago.

*NGOZI:* Adaeze, my daughter.

*ADAEZE:* Mama? Mama! Is that you?

*NGOZI:* Yes, my child. I have been watching you from the world of spirits. You have a pure heart. You saved Zara. That is true love, not selfish love. The river loves a pure heart.

*MAMALA:* Ngozi! You cannot save her! She broke the law!

*NGOZI:* No, Mamala. She followed the highest law — love. River God! Come and see what your bride did!

*NARRATOR:* The RIVER GOD appeared, tall and shining. He saw Zara, now healed and smiling. He saw Emeka who still waited after two years. He saw Adaeze who risked her throne to save a child.

*RIVER GOD:* Mamala, leave them. Adaeze has shown me what human love means. It is not selfish. It gives.

*MAMALA:* But you promised me she would die if she went to land!

*RIVER GOD:* I was jealous. I was wrong. Adaeze, you saved a child. You did not use your night for yourself. For that, I will forgive you.

*ADAEZE:* Thank you, my lord.

*RIVER GOD:* Tonight, I give you a new gift. You can be human for one full night. No curse. You and Emeka can be husband and wife till morning. And little Zara will never be sick again.

*LITTLE ZARA:* Thank you, Mama Adaeze!

*NARRATOR:* Mamala was angry and disappeared into the deep water forever.

*NGOZI:* My daughter, I am proud of you. Be happy tonight. (Her spirit disappears)

*NARRATOR:* Amara, who was watching from the bush, saw everything. She started crying and left quietly. She understood that Emeka and Adaeze's love was true.

*AMARA:* I will find my own love. Let them be happy.

*NARRATOR:* That night, Adaeze and Emeka finally became husband and wife by the river side, under the moon. Okonkwo played music and Zara danced.

It was their last night as humans, but it was the most beautiful night in Umunzu.

But in the morning, Adaeze had to return to the river...

*TO BE CONTINUED IN RIVER BRIDE PART 3...*

THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.t: THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.short: Morning has come. Adaeze must return to river forever after one night as Emeka's wife. But Mamala returns from deep water to flood Umunzu and kill Zara. Will River God finally free Adaeze?
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.long: Morning after one night as husband and wife. Adaeze must return to river forever. Mamala did not disappear in Part 2 - hid in deep water for revenge and floods Umunzu. Zara trapped on rock, Obinna house flooding, Igwe Okoro shouting. Adaeze powerless as human. Priestess Nneka tries to stop Mamala, mother ghost NGOZI returns stronger. River God appears angry, turns Mamala to stone forever at river bottom. Frees Adaeze to be human forever, gives double wedding Adaeze/Emeka and Amara/Okonkwo. Mamala stone gives healing power.
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.full:
*SYNOPSIS:*
The morning has come. Adaeze must return to the river forever after her one night as Emeka's wife. But Mamala returns from deep water to flood Umunzu and kill Zara. Will River God finally free Adaeze?

*FULL STORY PART 3 - FINAL:*

NARRATOR: Morning was coming in Umunzu. Sun was rising over the river. Birds were singing. Adaeze and Emeka were still by the riverbank, holding each other. Their one night as husband and wife was finished.

ADAEZE: Emeka, sun is coming. I must return. River God said I have till morning. Morning has come.

EMEKA: No! I will not let you go! Last night you were my wife! You slept in my arms! Now you want to leave me again to be queen of water?

ADAEZE: If I don't go, he will be angry. He will punish the village.

EMEKA: Then let him punish me! I will enter river with you! If you go, I go! Even if I drown!

NARRATOR: Inside the river, someone heard that. It was MAMALA. She did not disappear forever in Part 2. She hid in deep water, waiting for revenge.

MAMALA: (From deep water, angry) So she enjoyed one night? Good! Now I will destroy everything she loves! I will flood Umunzu!

NARRATOR: Suddenly, river started shaking. Water rose very fast. It was flooding.

OKONKWO: (Running) Emeka! Flood! Water is entering village!

IGWE OKORO: (Shouting from village square) Everyone run! River is angry again! Take your children!

OBINNA: (Adaeze's mother, crying) Adaeze! Where are you! Water is taking my house!

LITTLE ZARA: (Screaming, trapped on small rock in river) Mama Adaeze! Help! Water is carrying me!

ADAEZE: Zara! Mama Obinna!

EMEKA: We must save them! But I cannot swim fast!

NARRATOR: Adaeze tried to use her power, but she was now weak. She was almost human. She could not stop flood.

ADAEZE: I have no power! I am human now!

MAMALA: (Appearing from flood with snakes in hair, laughing) Yes! You are human now! Weak! Watch me drown your Zara! Watch me kill your village! This is what happens when you steal my husband's love!

NARRATOR: At that moment, PRIESTESS NNEKA came running from shrine with her white chalk and palm leaves.

PRIESTESS NNEKA: Mamala! Stop! The river has taken enough! I am Priestess of this land! I command you by the old gods! Stop!

MAMALA: You? Small priestess? You have no power over me!

NARRATOR: Then, bright white light appeared over the flooded river. It was NGOZI, Adaeze's mother ghost, shining stronger than ever before.

NGOZI: Mamala! Leave my daughter and my people!

MAMALA: Ngozi! You again! You are dead!

NGOZI: I am dead, but mother love never dies. River God! Come and see what your first wife is doing to innocent children!

NARRATOR: RIVER GOD appeared from water, very tall, his golden crown shining, his eyes red with anger. Water stopped shaking when he came.

RIVER GOD: Mamala! What are you doing?! In Part 2, I forgave Adaeze because she showed true love! I gave them one night! Why are you flooding humans again?!

MAMALA: Because you love her more than me! For 100 years I was queen! You never gave me one night on land!

RIVER GOD: I gave you palace! I gave you power! But you never learned to give, only to take! You want to kill a child Zara? For that, you will no longer be queen! You will become stone at bottom of river! Forever! People will see you as warning!

MAMALA: No! My lord! Please! Noooo!

NARRATOR: River God raised his hand. Thunder shouted. Mamala screamed as her blue body turned to stone. Snakes turned to rocks. She sank to bottom of river and became rock forever, with eyes open, lying under water. Flood stopped immediately. Water went back to normal. Zara was safe.

LITTLE ZARA: (Coughing but alive) Mama Adaeze! Water left!

ADAEZE: (Hugging Zara) Zara! You are alive!

OBINNA: My daughter! (Runs and hugs Adaeze)

IGWE OKORO: The flood has stopped! The river is calm! Priestess Nneka, thank the gods!

PRIESTESS NNEKA: It is not me, Igwe. It is true love that calmed river.

NARRATOR: River God looked at Adaeze and Emeka holding each other, wet from flood. He looked at Ngozi spirit, Obinna mother, and little Zara.

RIVER GOD: Adaeze... In Part 1, I took you because I was lonely. In Part 2, you risked everything to save a child Zara, not yourself. You showed me what human love means. It gives. It does not take.

ADAEZE: My lord...

RIVER GOD: Today, I free you. You are no longer River Bride. You are human forever. You will marry your Emeka. You will have children. You will grow old and die as human. And my river will never take a bride again. Rain will come every year in Umunzu because you taught me love.

EMEKA: (Kneeling, crying) Thank you! Thank you, River God!

RIVER GOD: And for Mamala's evil, I will make her stone give healing power. Any sick child who touches river where she lies will be healed.

NGOZI: (Smiling and fading slowly) My daughter, I am proud. My work is done. I can rest now in peace. Be happy, Adaeze. Tell Obinna I love her.

OBINNA: Ngozi? My sister? I hear you!

NGOZI: (Disappears forever, with light)

RIVER GOD: (To Emeka) Take care of her, hunter. (Slowly turns to water and disappears)

NARRATOR: That evening, Igwe Okoro made the biggest feast in Umunzu history. Drums were beating. Women were dancing. Adaeze wore her mother's white wrapper. Emeka wore his hunter best cloth with leopard skin.

IGWE OKORO: Today, we have two weddings! Adaeze and Emeka! And my daughter Amara and Okonkwo!

AMARA: (Shy, holding Okonkwo hand) I finally found love that loves me back.

OKONKWO: And I will love you forever, Amara.

NARRATOR: Priestess Nneka blessed both couples. Little Zara danced in middle.

ADAEZE: (Looking at river) Emeka, I was River Bride for two years, but I will be your wife for life.

EMEKA: And I waited for you at river for two years, and I will wait for you forever.

NARRATOR: And so, story of River Bride ended. Not with death, but with love winning. Every year, Adaeze and Emeka go to river and drop white flowers where River God disappeared. And deep at bottom, Mamala stone still lies, watching, but can never hurt anyone again.

THE END.

*A GHANAIAN FOLKLORE - 2026*
